brief: Whole New York Times parcel: cruciform glass shaft, white ceramic veil fading above the roof, exposed bracing,319m mast and open planted courtyard.

appearance.identity: Light ceramic screen over a cruciform glass tower, exposed steel corners, slender mast and low eastern podium with woodland court.
appearance.scope: Complete medium-fi parcel exterior retains the cruciform228m shaft, mapped western glass strip, eastern courtyard-preserving podium,260m fading ceramic screen and319m mast. Original125459-triangle recipe is preserved unchanged in Git. Reviewed source adds omitted western glass part260282089 and the courtyard grove of paper birches, sedge hillocks and timber path described and photographed by HMWhite. Nine reconstructed trees are an illustrative grove, not a counted vegetation survey; birch height15.24m follows published50ft. Original facade rods, brackets and structural beams remain in the detailed source. Ceramic rods use the existing shared tile_ceramic coating instead of granite; tile pattern is a generic shared coating, not a photographed rod. Screen bases follow mapped6m north/south and12m east/west min_height values; historic2007 photos are distinguished from current mapped state. Source facade pitch, rod count, specific support connections, door hardware and grove layout are reconstructed. Browser closeup replaces rod cylinders with double-sided strips of identical diameter and row schedule; street uses coarser strips and merged curtain-wall bars; district merges screen rods into wider low-frequency strips. Skyline keeps courtyard void, full shaft, fading crown supports and mast. No embedded textures. Interiors, tenant signage and temporary barriers omitted. Ground grade, night and physical-device performance unmeasured. Skyline uses5.2m-pitch screen strips with fading coverage and a2.6m geometric allowance; district/street bracket and brace plates replace small beam thicknesses. Generic shared ceramic coating tints are raised to pale white; glass remains a muted palette material.
